learningObjective: Contrast CPU SIMD lane execution with GPU SIMT warp execution, identifying differences in divergence handling, thread identity and programming model.
stem: Which of the following statements distinguishing CPU SIMD (e.g., AVX-512) from NVIDIA GPU SIMT (warp-based) execution are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: SIMT presents each warp lane as an independently addressable thread with its own program counter view (post-Volta), while SIMD lanes share one architectural instruction pointer and are handled explicitly by the programmer or compiler as vector data.

In SIMT, control-flow divergence within a warp is resolved by hardware serialization of taken/not-taken paths, whereas SIMD lanes rely on programmer-written masking (predication) to emulate divergent control.
SIMD guarantees higher peak throughput than SIMT on the same silicon area because SIMT wastes ~30% of area on per-thread state.
SIMT and SIMD are the same execution model with different names; the choice of terminology is purely marketing.

explanation: A: Under SIMT, each thread of a warp has an independent logical program state; post-Volta CUDA GPUs support independent thread scheduling with per-thread PCs and reconvergence. SIMD lanes share a single instruction pointer and are packed into wide vector registers manipulated by explicit instructions. B: SIMT hardware handles branch divergence via masking + serialization of divergent sides; SIMD requires the compiler/programmer to write predicated code (e.g., mask registers on AVX-512). C is false — throughput comparisons depend on many factors (memory bandwidth, precision, occupancy); no such generic silicon-area rule applies. D is false — the models differ in programming abstraction, divergence handling and thread-identity semantics.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: SIMT exposes threads as first-class entities with independent state (especially post-Volta), while SIMD packs lanes into a single instruction.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: hardware-managed divergence in SIMT vs software-managed predication in SIMD is a canonical distinction.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: peak throughput comparisons are workload- and architecture-specific; there is no universal SIMD > SIMT silicon efficiency claim.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: the models differ meaningfully in abstraction (threads vs lanes), divergence handling and programming interface.

assumptions: GPU baseline is Volta+ NVIDIA SIMT with independent thread scheduling.
CPU SIMD baseline is AVX-512 or similar wide-vector ISA with mask registers.
nonImplications: Does not imply SIMT eliminates divergence cost; divergence still serializes taken paths on GPUs.
Does not imply SIMD lanes cannot benefit from hardware-managed masking (some ISAs offer masks natively, e.g., AVX-512 k-registers).
